canonical_title: Anthropic plans enterprise data-retention shift allowing customer-controlled cloud storage
aliases: Anthropic enterprise data retention own cloud
treatment: Treat Enterprise Frontier Safeguards as officially announced and the earlier reported customer-controlled retention architecture as confirmed. Reinclude only for rollout start, broad availability, technical architecture changes, eligibility changes, material changes to the 30-day safety-monitoring requirement, or confirmed customer impact.
known_facts: Reuters reported on August 20 that Anthropic planned to retain the 30-day safety-monitoring requirement for advanced models while allowing business customers to keep the relevant data on their own cloud infrastructure.
On September 1 Anthropic officially announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), confirming the customer-controlled cloud storage design.
EFS combines zero-data-retention-style privacy with automated misuse monitoring across rolling traffic windows; flags go directly to the customer and no Anthropic human review is required by default.
Customer-owned storage, customer-managed encryption keys and fully automated review are opt-in and do not change model behavior, API pricing or rate limits.
Anthropic says EFS will support Claude Code, Claude Enterprise, Claude Platform, Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry.
EFS will roll out in phases starting later in fall 2026; eligible customers receive zero data retention on Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 until EFS is available.
Anthropic says EFS was developed with more than 100 customers and cloud partners across regulated industries.
reinclude_only_if: Anthropic begins the phased EFS rollout or announces broad availability.
The 30-day monitoring/retention requirement is materially shortened, extended, removed, or given new exceptions.
Anthropic publishes material technical architecture, audit, security or compliance details for EFS.
Eligibility, supported surfaces, pricing or model behavior materially changes.
A major enterprise customer confirms a material deployment, privacy, compliance, or availability consequence.
notes: FOLLOW_UP on 2026-09-02 JST. 前回からの差分: the previously reported plan is now an official product called Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, with supported platforms, customer-side human review, opt-in storage/encryption controls and a phased fall rollout explicitly documented.
